title: Mastermind: How to Think Like Sherlock Holmes

questions.q: Which of the brain’s two systems do we use by default?
a: The reflexive system, which accepts the first answer it finds
The conscious system, which questions every assumption
The memory system, which replays past experiences
The emotional system, which ignores logic entirely
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the brain is wired to save energy, so the reflexive system takes the first answer as correct.

questions.q: What does mindfulness require, according to the summary?
a: Energy and focus to stay aware of the present moment
Complete silence and isolation from other people
Memorizing facts before attempting to reason
Trusting your first impression without hesitation
questions.why: Lesson 1 notes that engaging the conscious system takes energy and focus, which is why it feels difficult.

questions.q: What is Holmes’s “attic” metaphor meant to explain?
a: The mind stores both content and the structures used to organize it
The brain has a fixed capacity that fills up permanently
Memories are stored randomly and cannot be arranged
Only urgent information deserves a place in memory
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes the attic as holding experiences and knowledge plus the structures you use to store them.

Choosing the option that is most widely available in stores
Believing information simply because an expert said it
Preferring the first explanation you hear over later ones
questions.why: Lesson 3 defines it as deciding based on how much information you can readily remember.

questions.q: What should you do to counter your biases before making a decision?
a: Gather all the information and question your own patterns
Rely on your first impression to avoid overthinking
Ask only people who already agree with you
Decide quickly so doubt cannot interfere
questions.why: Lesson 3 advises forcing objectivity, having all the information and doubting yourself to spot biased patterns.
